name: Rockwell Commander 112/114
summary: Rockwell's four-seat, low-wing, retractable-gear single (1972–80), later built by Commander Aircraft; known for a roomy cabin and rugged build.

engines: Single Lycoming flat-four or flat-six in a blunt, deep cowl

tellTales: Low-wing retractable with a deep, wide cabin and bulky nose
Stout, short fuselage for a four-seater

confusedWith.howToTell: The Commander has a swept-back fin and a roomy cabin; the Mooney has a forward-swept fin and a narrow cabin.
The Commander has a bulkier cabin and a swept fin; the A36 has rear cargo doors and a squared tail.
The Commander has a deeper, shorter fuselage; the Viking has a very tall fin and a long, slim nose.
The Commander is an all-metal low-wing with retractable gear; the SR series is a composite, fixed-gear aircraft with a parachute hatch on the rear deck.
